name: Equator theory

lead: Equator theory is a framework posted on looksmax.org by a user who argues that attraction follows distance from the equator: people from hot regions are said to be drawn to the narrower, higher noses of cooler-climate populations, and vice versa. It is used as a way to estimate which kind of audience will respond most to a given phenotype.

The idea borrows from a real topic in anthropology, the variation of nose shape with climate. Researchers have discussed whether nose breadth adapted to temperature and humidity, but the forum theory about partner attraction itself has not been studied.

paras: Posters compare their own nasal index (nose width relative to height) and ancestral climate with that of people they find attractive, then discuss patterns in dating-app or forum anecdotes. It is a thinking tool for styling, grooming and self-assessment rather than a procedure.

The theory is built on anecdote and can lead people to overgeneralise from small samples or to discuss people in terms of ancestry. Wikipedia notes that mixed ancestry means nose shape does not neatly define populations.

angle.text: Followers use the framework to understand how their facial structure may read to different viewers and to set expectations about who responds to it. It informs how people think about presenting their features rather than altering them.

lead: Equator theory is a concept from the looksmaxxing forum looksmax.org that links facial structure, especially nose shape, to the climate of a person's ancestors and to who they tend to be attracted to. Its author presented it as a way to work out which women or men are most attracted to a given phenotype.[1] One thread frames it as: people with a broad (platyrrhine) nose are said to be more attracted to people with a narrow (leptorrhine) nose, and the poster asks whether the reverse also holds.[2]

Its appeal for self-improvement is practical: if attraction is partly relative to a viewer's own phenotype, a person can think about which features to emphasise, and which audience to expect a positive response from.

Anthropologists have independently discussed climate and nose form: Wikipedia reports hypotheses that nose size differences between populations may reflect adaptation to local temperature and humidity, with sexual selection possibly also involved.[3] No published study has tested the forum theory's claim about attraction.
infobox: Attraction is stronger toward partners from a different ancestral climate

paras: The theory as posted holds that the distance of one's ancestral home from the equator shapes facial features such as nose breadth, and that people tend to be attracted to features that differ from their own along that axis.[1][2]
Its author described the thread as written mainly for personal use and shared it for feedback, and a reply in the thread offered a counter-example of Nordic users who prefer similar partners.[1]

Proponents point to personal observations and to dating-forum examples they say fit the pattern.[1] In a second thread a poster reports that his own nasal index and his ancestry from a hot region did not line up neatly, and other users discussed whether a given nose is wide or narrow for its climate, showing how contested individual cases are in the community.[2]

The background anthropological idea is that nose size and shape varied with climate and may reflect adaptation to temperature and humidity, an idea discussed by researchers with differing views on specific cases such as Neanderthals.[3] The nasal index was introduced by Paul Topinard and was originally used in racial typologies; Wikipedia notes that because populations have mixed, nose shape does not define specific populations.[3]
Researchers have not published tests of whether people prefer partners with a nose shape different from their own climate group.

lore.intro: The theory circulates on looksmax.org in threads where users test it against their own nose measurements and dating experiences.[1][2]

claims.claim: People are most attracted to partners from a different ancestral climate than their own.
Broad-nosed (platyrrhine) people are more attracted to narrow-nosed (leptorrhine) people.
Nose shape reflects the climate of ancestors.
